messages:
maria (eng-runtime): Heads up — we just saw a 3-4x p99 spike on shared-gpu-pool-c between 08:24-08:27 UTC. Impacted small-chat models mostly. Anyone on call?

sam (eng-sre): saw the alert, looking. p99 went ~120ms -> ~480ms. No infra restarts.

dan (eng-ml): can you paste the kernel selection log for that window? suspect kernel flip thrash again.

maria (eng-runtime): pasting relevant snippets from runtime logs:

```
[08:24:03] kernel_switch: model=chat-small-v1 tenant=acme from=int8_fast -> fp16_generic reason=seqlen>1024 count=372
[08:24:05] batch_autoscale: pool=shared-c new_batch=256 old_batch=64 reason=queue-len>threshold
[08:24:06] kvcache_evict: pool=shared-c evicted_slots=1823 policy=LRU per_tenant_limit=512
[08:24:07] schedule_lock_ms=145
```

maria (eng-runtime): full stack: kernel flips + batch blowup + kv cache evictions. looks like a feedback loop.

henry (eng-platform): that schedule_lock_ms number is concerning. Could be lock contention from per-batch merging.

dan (eng-ml): profiling-bot output for the time slice:

```
profiling-bot: cpu samples: attention_kernel_fp16 44.8%, kv_cache_reclaim 28.1%, scheduler_lock 13.7%, batching_logic 9.4%, others 4.0%
```

profiling-bot: flame link: https://internal.flames/1932456789 (private)

lisa (eng-runtime): confirmed tenant-level metrics: acme had a sudden burst (~3k concurrent requests) and kept pushing long sequence prompts. Their KV hit rate dropped from 98% -> 61% triggering evictions.

san (note: small typo fixed)

sam (eng-sre): did autoscaler kick? we should check if autoscale reduced pressure or made batching worse.

maria (eng-runtime): autoscaler increased batch target to keep throughput, but that increased serialization latency when attention kernel switched to fp16_generic which is slower per-token at those seqlen shapes.

dan (eng-ml): root cause hypothesis: long-seq tenant causes kernel_autoswitch -> kernel slower + large batches -> kv cache eviction -> model warmup misses -> more seqlen requests queued -> autoscale increases batch -> loop. Noisy neighbor effect.

henry (eng-platform): agree. quick mitigation suggestions:
- pin noisy tenant to per-tenant concurrency cap (soft cap 300)
- temporarily disable kernel_autoswitch for shared pools (fallback to stable kernel)
- cap batch growth to 128 when p99>200ms

lisa (eng-runtime): I'll open a config PR for per-tenant caps and batch cap. assigning to @henry to deploy quick flag.

maria (eng-runtime): @dan can you reproduce locally with replay of acme trace? if we can get a repro we can test kernel thresholds.

dan (eng-ml): already on it — running the trace replay with seqlen distribution and KV hit emulation. preliminary run shows kernel switch threshold at 1024 is too aggressive for this model. lowering to 2048 avoids flip and keeps p99 ~140ms.

```
# repro command
./replay_trace --trace acme_burst.json --pool shared-c --seqlen-threshold 1024
```

sam (eng-sre): I've created an incident page and tagged pg: https://incidents/local/INC-1932456789

profiling-bot: note: kvcache_evict rate correlated with tenants using shared-kv-slot-policy V2.

maria (eng-runtime): action items:
- henry: deploy soft per-tenant concurrency cap + batch cap flag now (low risk)
- dan: finish repro and post perf profile comparing 1024 vs 2048 kernel threshold
- lisa: add alert for kernel_switch_rate > 10/min and kvcache_eviction_rate > 100/min per-pool
- sam: update incident page and hold until metrics stabilize

henry (eng-platform): pushing flag now (will update in 60s).

[~60s later]
henry (eng-platform): deployed flags: per_tenant_cap=300, batch_growth_cap=128, kernel_autoswitch_disabled_for(shared-c)=true

maria (eng-runtime): metrics look better already. p99 back down to ~160ms, kv evictions dropping. thanks.

dan (eng-ml): repro confirms: no kernel flip at 2048 threshold, batch growth stays moderate, kv hit rate ~95%. I'll put up a change proposal to make threshold model-aware rather than global.

lisa (eng-runtime): will add the alerts and a runbook note about kernel-autoswitch tradeoffs.

sam (eng-sre): closing incident once 30m stable. adding postmortem stub now.

maria (eng-runtime): quick notes for postmortem: noisy tenant with long sequences triggered kernel-selection thrash + batching heuristics that prioritize throughput -> created a latency amplification loop and kv cache thrash. Temporary mitigations applied; long-term: model-aware kernel thresholds, per-tenant cache quotas, and batch-growth backpressure when latency rises.

profiling-bot: saved profile 1932456789 to /profiles/1932456789/profile.pb

maria (eng-runtime): thanks all. follow-ups assigned. :)
